en: The Path of Discrimination 1,
Great Chapter 1.8.
Discourse on the Perversions (Vipallāsakathā)
The Previous Introduction:
"Bhikkhus, there are these four perversions of perception, perversions of mind, and perversions of view.
What are the four?"
Monks, regarding the impermanent as permanent is a perversion of perception, a perversion of mind, and a perversion of view.
Monks, regarding suffering as happiness is a perversion of perception, a perversion of mind, and a perversion of view.
Monks, regarding the non-self as self is a perversion of perception, a perversion of mind, and a perversion of view.
“Bhikkhus, to perceive the beautiful in the ugly is a perversion of perception, a perversion of mind, and a perversion of view.
These, bhikkhus, are the four perversions of perception, perversions of mind, and perversions of view.
There are, bhikkhus, these four that are not perversions of perception, not perversions of mind, and not perversions of view.”
Which four?
Monks, regarding the impermanent as "impermanent" is the non-perversion of perception, the non-perversion of mind, and the non-perversion of view.
Regarding the suffering as "suffering" is the non-perversion of perception, the non-perversion of mind, and the non-perversion of view.
“Monks, regarding what is non-self, the perception that it is ‘non-self’ is not a perversion of perception, not a perversion of mind, and not a perversion of view.
Regarding what is foul, the perception that it is ‘foul’ is not a perversion of perception, not a perversion of mind, and not a perversion of view.
These, monks, are the four things that are not perversions of perception, not perversions of mind, and not perversions of view.”
“Perceiving the impermanent as permanent,
perceiving suffering as happiness,
and perceiving what is non-self as self— ”
Perceiving the foul as beautiful,
beings are struck down by wrong view,
their minds distracted and their perceptions distorted.
Those people who are joined to Māra and have not attained security from the yoke,
these beings go on in saṃsāra.
Those who go to birth and death.
And when Buddhas, the light-bringers, arise in the world;
They proclaim this Dhamma which leads to the stilling of suffering;
having heard it from them, those possessed of wisdom—
Having regained their own minds,
they saw the impermanent as impermanent and saw suffering as suffering.
Seeing the non-self as non-self,
and the foul as foul—
by undertaking right view, [one attains the goal].
“He has transcended all suffering.
Regarding these four perversions, for a person endowed with right view, which have been abandoned and which have not been abandoned?
Some have been abandoned, and some have not been abandoned.
The perversion of perception, the perversion of mind, and the perversion of view that take the impermanent to be permanent have been abandoned.
The perversion of perception, the perversion of mind, and the perversion of view that take the painful to be pleasant have been abandoned.
The perversion of perception, the perversion of mind, and the perversion of view that take the non-self to be self have been abandoned.
The perception of the beautiful arises regarding the unattractive; the mind arises [thus]; the perversion of view is abandoned.
Regarding two bases, all six perversions are abandoned.
Regarding two bases, two perversions are abandoned and four perversions are not abandoned.
Regarding the four bases, eight perversions have been abandoned and four perversions have not been abandoned.
The Discussion on Perversions is finished.
